name: Garage Addition vs Garage Conversion vs Garage Remodel

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between a garage addition, garage conversion, and garage remodel in Los Angeles County?
mainEntity.text: What is the difference between a garage addition, garage conversion, and garage remodel in Los Angeles County?

acceptedAnswer.text: These three project types are often confused, but they involve different scopes. A garage addition means creating new garage square footage, such as adding a detached structure or enlarging an attached garage. A garage conversion means changing an existing garage into living space, a rental unit, office, or other use. A garage remodel keeps the garage functioning as a garage but may include new doors, insulation, flooring, lighting, storage, drywall, or electrical upgrades. In Los Angeles County, the distinction matters because permit requirements, zoning review, and building code compliance can change based on the project type. For example, a conversion may require more insulation, fire separation, ventilation, and egress considerations than a basic remodel. Homeowners should define the goal clearly before getting bids, because contractors price and design each of these projects differently.
acceptedAnswer.description: A garage addition builds new garage space, a garage conversion changes an existing garage into another use, and a garage remodel updates an existing garage without changing its core use. In Los Angeles County, the permits, structural requirements, and costs can be very different for each project type.
